description: The Insurance Sector is a crucial pillar of the Indian Economy, providing financial security and risk management. It is regulated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), which ensures the orderly growth of the industry and protects policyholders' interests.

sections.title: Meaning and Historical Background of Insurance
sections.description: The evolution of the insurance sector in India, its fundamental principles, and the key milestones of nationalisation.

key_concepts.explanation: A legal contract where one party (insurer) promises to compensate the other party (insured) against a specified future financial loss in exchange for a fixed premium.

The practice where an insurance company transfers a portion of its risk portfolios to another major insurance company (reinsurer) to reduce the likelihood of paying a large obligation resulting from an insurance claim.

historical_events.significance: Established in Calcutta, it was the first life insurance company to be set up in India.
The Government of India merged 245 Indian and foreign insurers to form the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to spread life insurance widely, especially to rural areas.
The General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act was passed, merging 107 insurers to form the General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) and its four subsidiaries.

sections.title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
sections.description: The establishment, composition, and core functions of the apex regulatory body of the Indian insurance sector.

key_concepts.explanation: Headed by former RBI Governor R.N. Malhotra, this committee's recommendations led to the opening of the insurance sector to private players and paved the way for the establishment of IRDAI.

historical_events.significance: Passed by the Parliament, granting IRDA the status of an independent statutory body.
IRDAI formally began its operations to regulate, promote, and ensure orderly growth of the insurance and reinsurance business in India.

important_facts.fact: The headquarters of IRDAI is located in Hyderabad, Telangana. It was shifted from New Delhi in 2001.
IRDAI is a 10-member body comprising a Chairman, 5 whole-time members, and 4 part-time members, all appointed by the Government of India.
The Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) limit in the Indian insurance sector has been increased from 49% to 74% under the automatic route.

sections.title: Types of Insurance and Products
sections.description: The broad classification of insurance policies and their specific financial and protective objectives.

key_concepts.explanation: A contract that guarantees a lump sum payment to the nominee upon the death of the insured or upon the maturity of the policy term, ensuring long-term financial security.
Encompasses all types of insurance other than life insurance, such as health, motor, fire, and marine insurance, which provide compensation for specific damages or losses.
A financial product that offers the dual benefit of life insurance cover and market-linked wealth creation (investment) in a single integrated plan.

sections.title: Major Public Sector Insurance Companies
sections.description: Key insurance and reinsurance entities wholly or partially owned by the Government of India.

key_associations.extra_info: It is India's largest life insurance company and the largest institutional investor; headquartered in Mumbai.

key_associations.item: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)
key_associations.extra_info: It is the sole domestic reinsurance company operating in the Indian insurance market; headquartered in Mumbai.
It is primarily responsible for implementing the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY).

important_facts.fact: There are four major public sector general insurance companies in India: National Insurance (NICL), New India Assurance (NIACL), Oriental Insurance (OICL), and United India Insurance (UIICL).
New India Assurance Company Limited (NIACL) is the largest general insurance company in India.

sections.title: Key Government Insurance Schemes
sections.description: Flagship social security and financial inclusion schemes launched by the Government of India to provide affordable insurance coverage.

key_associations.item: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
key_associations.extra_info: For citizens aged 18-50 years; provides a life cover of Rs. 2 lakh for death due to any reason at an annual premium of Rs. 436.
For citizens aged 18-70 years; provides a cover of Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability at a nominal annual premium of Rs. 20.

key_associations.item: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
key_associations.extra_info: It is the world's largest fully government-funded health insurance scheme, providing a cashless cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
